title: The Sanitation Strike
subtitle: Garbage crews strike in dengue season; the hospital is already full
coldOpen: Day three of a sanitation strike over safety gear.
07:00. Dengue admissions are up forty percent.
Garbage is piling up outside the hospital gate.

briefing.grievance: Sanitation workers want gloves, boots and a pay slip that matches their hours. They have asked for a year. Meanwhile, standing waste breeds the mosquitoes filling the wards.
knownFacts: Crews have had no protective gear issued since last year.
Dengue admissions are up 40% in two weeks.
Waste has not been collected for three days.
unverifiedClaims: A post says the union is being paid by a private waste firm.
A message says the city will fire all strikers tomorrow.
briefing.responsibility: You run the city’s sanitation and the hospital liaison. The workers’ grievance and the public’s health are both real.
briefing.objective: Get the gear and the hours on paper, get the waste moving, and keep a lawful strike from becoming a firing.

rightsMoments.question: Sanitation workers are on a lawful strike during a disease outbreak. What is the proportionate response?

options.text: Meet the grievance and agree a minimum service for health-critical routes, rather than banning the strike outright.
options.feedback: Correct. Essential needs can be protected by a minimum service; a blanket ban or mass firing is disproportionate.

options.text: Fire everyone who does not return within the hour.
options.feedback: Mass termination for a lawful strike is punitive and leaves the service without crews.

options.text: Nothing can be done until the strike ends on its own.
options.feedback: Health-critical routes can be covered by agreement or volunteers without breaking the strike.

rightsMoments.principle: Workers may associate and strike lawfully (Article 19(1)(c)); restrictions must be reasonable and proportionate. Essential needs are met by narrow measures, not by punishing the whole workforce.
rightsMoments.why: The workers asked for gloves that were sitting in a store; a minimum service kept the hospital clean while the grievance was met.

simple.question: Garbage workers are on a lawful strike during a disease outbreak. What is the fair response?

options.a: Fix their complaint and run the hospital routes by agreement.
options.b: Fire everyone who does not return within an hour.
options.c: Do nothing until the strike ends.

feedback.a: Yes! Meet the need and protect the urgent routes.
feedback.b: No. Firing everyone is unfair and leaves nobody to work.
feedback.c: Urgent routes can run without breaking the strike.

simple.principle: Workers may strike lawfully. Protect urgent needs with small, fair steps, not by punishing everyone.
simple.why: The gloves were sitting in a store. A minimum service kept the hospital clean while the complaint was fixed.

closing.good: The gloves came out of the store, the hospital gate was clean by evening, and the crews came back under a deal they signed.
closing.mixed: The hospital was cleared, but the crews are still waiting for the audit and the gear list is only half issued.
closing.poor: The strike was broken instead of answered, and the piles are still there with new names on the trucks.
